chapter.title: The Aquarium Is Closed
chapter.goal: Steve wants to find out what happened to Nora.

c2_aquarium.coach: Some leads come with recordings. Listen, or read the sound traces: a sound that repeats looks the same each time.
c2_aquarium.objective: Get into the sealed north wing. The work order carries Nora’s staff credential.
notes: Iris (still shown as Nora’s copy) and Lyle arrive in the departure, which leads straight into c2_ship.

intro.text: Emergency. Bellwether beach. People are walking into the water, and they’re not coming back out. Hello? Hello?
intro.direction: on his flip phone, static rising

intro.text: The line died. I didn’t know if anyone had heard.

intro.new: steve|There was one place in town with Nora’s name on it that night. The north wing of her aquarium.
steve|I knew the back way in. Four years of visiting her at work.

plan.title: The old exhibit plan
plan.goal: Find a way into the sealed north wing.
plan.background: The north wing has been closed to the public for two years. On the old plan, the café and the public tank lead to the visitor hall, and door 1 goes from there to the north wing. A newer notice taped over the plan says door 1 is bricked up. The service door opens into the pump room, which has three pipes.

lead.text: Nora showed me this plan the week I fixed the underwater speakers. She said the pumps were the heartbeat of the place.

lead: steve|On the old plan, the café and the public tank lead to the visitor hall. Door one leads to the north wing.
steve|But this newer notice says door one is bricked up. The service door still opens into the pump room.
steve|And the notice says to follow the one pipe that carries water away from the pump.
plan.prompt: The old plan and the newer notice disagree. Which route still reaches the north wing?
plan.instruction: Trust the newer notice. Door 1 is bricked up, so the visitor hall goes nowhere. The service door opens into the pump room. Pump arrows: pipe N flows in, pipe E flows out, pipe S flows in.

rows.label: Which way in?
rows.feedback: That visitor plan predates the brickwork. Which entrance still opens straight into the pump room?

rows.label: Which pump-room pipe?
rows.feedback: Hang on. The arrows on N and S point back at the pump. I need a pipe leading away from it.

hints: Where the old plan and the new notice disagree, trust the notice.
Door 1 is bricked up, so the visitor hall is a dead end. Which entrance skips the visitor hall?
In the pump room, look for the one arrow that points away from the pump.
lines: steve|Service door, pump room, the outgoing pipe. Into the north wing.
plan.finding: steve|The way in runs from the service door through the pump room, along the only pipe that carries water away.

guard.title: Two service doors
guard.goal: Pick the corridor with nobody in it.
guard.background: Steve hears a voice and footsteps behind each door. On the kitchen tapes, even the breath before Nora’s greeting matched across two different mornings. He listens for that kind of repetition here.
lead: steve|Someone’s behind both doors. Maybe only one of them is real.
steve|A real person never steps or coughs the same way twice. A recording does it every time.
steve|Six seconds at each door. Then I compare the two.
guard.prompt: Steve records six seconds at each door. Which corridor can he cross without meeting anyone?

wrong.0: Those footsteps change their spacing. Somebody real is walking that corridor.
wrong.2: Neither door goes quiet. One of them never will, because it’s on a loop.

hints: Look for a sound that repeats on the same beat.
Compare the spacing and shape of the peaks in each six-second strip.
Watch the bell and the cough. In one strip they come back on exactly the same beat. Nobody coughs on a schedule.
lines: c2_aquarium.guard.01
guard.finding: steve|The filter corridor plays a loop: the same bell and the same cough on the same beat. Nobody’s there. The pump corridor has real footsteps.

intercom.title: Nora’s coat and the intercom tape
intercom.goal: Work out what Nora’s tape means.
intercom.background: Behind new plywood: holding rooms, cots and, on a hook, Nora’s real aquarium fleece with every enamel fish pin. In the pocket is a spool from the old intercom, dated May 29 in Nora’s handwriting. A loose duplicate in the drawer holds only her two whistle notes. Tonight is October 22.
lead: steve|Her fleece. Her real fleece, with the fish pins. And an intercom spool.
steve|The paper on the spool is dated in her handwriting. May 29th.
steve|Her second note goes up. Like it always did, before this summer.
steve|And there’s a loose copy of the whistle in the drawer. On that one, the second note falls.
intercom.prompt: Nora’s voice, Nora’s whistle, and a date on the spool. What does the tape tell Steve?

board.instruction: Use the tape and what Steve learned on Sunday to answer four questions.
evidence: Nora dated the spool in her own handwriting: May 29.
On Sunday, Nora’s family said she changed at the end of May.
Nora’s second whistle note rises on the spool and falls on the loose copy in the drawer.
On the pier, Admiral turned away from a whistle whose second note fell.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: When was the real Nora last here?
How long has someone else lived Nora’s life?
Which whistle did Admiral turn away from?
pieces: The loose copy: second note falls

board.wrong_text: Steve stares at the spool. Something here doesn’t fit yet.

hints: Start with the date on the spool. Then count the months to tonight.
Count the months from late May to late October, one at a time.
Admiral comes to Nora’s real whistle. On the pier he turned away from a whistle whose second note fell.
lines: c2_aquarium.out.02
c2_aquarium.intercom.02
intercom.finding: steve|The real Nora recorded this here on May 29. Someone else has been living her life with me for five months. Her whistle rises. The one Admiral ignored falls.

recap: steve|The north wing is no repair job. It’s a holding station, with cots, Nora’s real coat, and her voice on a tape from May.
steve|Nora was here, whistling for help. I didn’t hear her for five months.
outro: lyle_copy|Easy now, Steve. Nobody wants this to be hard.
lyle_copy|The old intake is open. I have the service key. This way.
c2_aquarium.next: Through the old seawater intake tunnel, under the bay (c2_ship).

c2_ship.coach: Turn on Show reel transcripts if you would rather read the recordings than listen.
c2_ship.objective: Get out of the scan chair before it finishes. Then find the real Nora.
notes: Lead c2_ship.intake is the brass intake hatch in the foreground floor. Steve walks to it past the attendant, who stands at the speaker column after the release.
Nora's copy and Lyle are dismissed at the end of the command lead and leave when the command lead is done. Only the attendant is there for the escape.
Saren is heard only over the intercom here. His release command is the fixed recording recording.release.
Film after the departure: a tank fills around a shape grown from the 61 percent memory index. Binding completes offscreen. Steve never sees it.

intro.new: steve|Lyle unlocked the old intake and walked me down the tunnel under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.
steve|Glass corridors. Slow light. And a hum that was almost a tune.

intro: guard|“You are the author of your own story.” This is from a human book. Is it helping?
guard|The memory index opens with the oldest records. Binding runs separately. Here is your driving test. Congratulations. You passed.

command.title: The intercom
command.goal: Get the exact command that opens the chair onto Dad’s tape.
command.background: Steve is strapped into the chair, and Dad’s recorder is running in his cardigan pocket. When a strap sticks, the attendant asks for a release and nothing happens. Then a calm voice on the intercom, the Prefect, gives the command, and the buckle opens. The cassette keeps turning onto blank tape after the click.
lead: guard|This restraint is sticking. Release, please.
guard|Thank you, Prefect. And fastened again.

lead.new: steve|Dad’s recorder was running in my pocket the whole time.
steve|The chair’s little lamp stayed dark when the attendant asked. It lit up for the voice on the intercom.
steve|Dad’s counter ticks once a second. The lamp lit at tick three. The buckle clicked at tick seven.
steve|The tape keeps moving after the click. Blank tape, not leader. There’s room left.
guard|Thank you, escorts. It is nearly dawn, and the town will expect you at breakfast.
lead.direction: to Nora’s copy and the deputy, sending them back up the tunnel

command.prompt: Steve has the moment on tape. Which voice opens the chair, and how long is the command?

board.instruction: Use the chair’s lamp and the tape counter to answer four questions.
evidence: When the attendant asked for a release, the chair’s lamp stayed dark.
The lamp lit at tick 3, on the Prefect’s first word, “Release.”
The buckle clicked at tick 7, just after his last word, “authorization.”
The tape counter ticks once a second.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Which voice does the chair obey?

board.wrong_text: Something here doesn’t match the lamp or the counter yet.

hints: The lamp only lights for one of the two voices.
The command starts when the lamp lights and ends when the buckle clicks.
Count the ticks from the lamp to the buckle. Each tick is one second.
command.finding: steve|The Prefect’s release command is on Dad’s tape: four seconds, from “Release” to the click.

escape.title: The scan chair
escape.goal: Open the chair with the Prefect’s own voice.
escape.background: Nora’s copy and Lyle have gone back up the tunnel to town, and the scan has started again. The attendant stands by the chair with a slate. Dad’s cassette caught three voices tonight: Nora’s intercom spool playing in the north wing, the attendant, and the Prefect’s four-second command. Steve still has the original spool. He can reach two microphone grilles. The attendant tested the hall speakers on the cracked grille. When Steve’s sleeve brushed the whole grille, the chair’s lamp blinked. The chair only listens while its lamp is lit.
lead: guard|Fifty-eight percent. Fifty-nine. You are doing very well.
steve|Dad’s recorder caught three voices tonight. Nora’s spool, the attendant, and the Prefect.
steve|Two speaker covers by my hand. The attendant tested the hall speakers on the cracked one.
steve|When my sleeve brushed the other grille, the chair’s lamp blinked.
steve|The lamp stays lit for one second each beat. At the notch marked sixty-one, it stays lit for six.
escape.prompt: Pick the recording, the grille and the moment.

rows.label: Which recording?
rows.feedback: The attendant talks to the chair, but whose voice did it actually take an order from?

rows.label: Which grille?
rows.feedback: The cracked grille made a noise in the hall. Which one made the lamp on my chair blink?

rows.label: When to press play?
rows.feedback: A regular blink buys me one second. I need four whole seconds for the command.

escape.instruction: The chair obeys the voice it has obeyed before. It hears only the grille that makes its lamp blink, and only while the lamp is lit. The lamp stays lit one second on a beat and six seconds at the 61 notch. The command takes four seconds.
hints: Which voice has this chair already obeyed?
The cracked grille only feeds the hall speakers. The other grille talks to the chair.
Four seconds will not fit in a one-second beat. Use the only longer window, from its start.

lines.direction: Dad’s recorder, held to the grille

lines.new: guard|Prefect? I did not ask for a release. The scan is not finished.
lines.direction: startled, turning away from the chair to the speaker column

lines.new: guard|Prefect, please repeat your instruction. The chair says you released it.
lines.direction: at the speaker column, back to the chair

lines.text: It worked. Index sixty-one percent, and all of me is getting out of this chair.

lines.new: steve|The attendant is busy arguing with the column. Quietly, now.

escape.finding: steve|The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair at the notch marked sixty-one. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent; whatever it could bind would come later.

nora.title: The amber sleeper
nora.goal: Find out whether the sleeper is alive.
nora.background: Beyond the chair is a hall of sleepers in amber light, hundreds of them. In one bed lies Nora. A light flashes down the corridor on a steady beat, and a pickup on the rail repeats each flash one second later. Steve can’t touch the glass without disturbing whatever keeps her there, so he timed three rhythms with his stopwatch.
lead: steve|Nora.

lead.new: steve|That hum. It’s almost a song. I know it from somewhere.

lead: steve|The corridor light flashes at two, six and ten seconds. Every four seconds, like a clock.
steve|The pickup on the rail repeats each flash, one second late.
steve|And there’s fog on the glass above her mouth. Three seconds, seven, then twelve.
steve|I made a rubbing of each rhythm. Now the labels have come off.
nora.prompt: Three timing rubbings lost their labels. Which one is Nora breathing?

board.instruction: Two rhythms keep the ship’s beat. One keeps its own time.
evidence: The corridor light flashed at seconds 2, 6 and 10.
The pickup on the rail repeats each flash one second later.
Fog above Nora’s mouth appeared at seconds 3, 7 and 12.
Strip A reads 2, 6, 10, strip B reads 3, 7, 11, and strip C reads 3, 7, 12.

stages.prompt: Put a label on each rhythm.
slots: Which strip is the corridor light?
Which strip is the rail pickup?

board.wrong_text: One of these rhythms doesn’t belong where you put it.

hints: Compare each strip with the flash times.
The rail pickup is each flash plus one second.
Nora’s breath is the one strip with an uneven gap at the end.
lines: steve|I can’t move you without stopping whatever keeps you breathing. I’m coming back for you.
c2_ship.nora.01
nora.finding: steve|Nora is alive. Her breath keeps its own time, a little behind the ship’s. She’s asleep, not gone.

intake.title: The intake hatch
intake.goal: Slip down the intake hatch and call Admiral through the old aquarium speakers.
intake.background: Steve creeps to the brass intake hatch while the attendant waits at the speaker column. Then the Prefect answers: he gave no release. The attendant turns and sees the empty chair. Steve hauls the valve wheel and drops into the intake tunnel, and the sea floods in behind him. The attendant wades in after him. The water is at Steve’s chest. The tunnel runs back to the aquarium, past the underwater speakers Steve repaired the day he met Nora. Admiral swims those waters every night. Steve has Nora’s intercom spool, the loose copy of her whistle from the drawer, and the Prefect’s command on Dad’s cassette.

lead.new: saren|I gave no release. Look at the chair.
guard|The chair is empty! Prefect, the human is gone!
lead.direction: whirling round from the speaker column

lead.new: steve|The brass hatch in the floor. That’s the intake valve. Flood the tunnel, and they’ll have to swim after me.
lead.direction: a whisper, hauling the valve wheel

lead.new: guard|Water in the intake! The human is in the tunnel!

lead.text: The tunnel’s flooding. The underwater speakers still work... I fixed them, the day I met her.

lead: steve|Admiral swims the whole bay at night. If he hears the right whistle, he’ll come.

lead.new: guard|Please stop! You are not finished!
lead.direction: wading into the tunnel after him

lead: steve|Nora’s spool, the loose copy, or the Prefect. One chance.
audition_labels: Spool B: the loose copy from the drawer
options: Spool B: the loose copy from the drawer

wrong.1: That’s the whistle Admiral turned away from on the pier.
wrong.2: His voice opens chairs. It won’t bring a sea lion.

hints: Who has never once ignored Nora’s real whistle?
Think back to the pier. Which whistle did Admiral turn away from?
Admiral answers the whistle whose second note rises. Which spool is that?

lines.new: steve|Come on, Admiral. You never missed this one.
guard|Something is in the water! Something big!

intake.finding: steve|Nora’s real whistle, through the speakers I fixed the day we met. Admiral came down through the dark and dragged me to the surface.

recap: steve|There is a ship under the bay. Nora is asleep on it, alive, with hundreds of others. At the far end of the hall, one bed lay under frost, and something too tall to be human slept in it. The guards never looked at it.
steve|They tried to make another me. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent. I didn’t know yet what the tank would bind from it.
steve|And the woman with Nora’s face, who locked me out on the balcony and then let me go, had walked me to that chair herself.

outro.new: steve|Sheriff... there’s a ship. Under the bay.
outro.direction: coughing up seawater on the beach at dawn

c2_ship.next: Chapter 2 film: dawn on the beach, then a tank filling aboard the ship. Then Chapter 3.

lines: steve|Where are we, Nor? What is this place?
iris|Somewhere safe, under the bay. Please don’t be frightened.
steve|You walked me down that tunnel yourself.
iris|They asked me to. I always do what I am asked.
steve|Do you remember the day we met?
iris|At the aquarium. You fixed the underwater speakers. You had a coffee stain on your green shirt.
steve|You remember the stain, too?
iris|I remember everything she saw. Everything I saw.
steve|Carmen keeps my plate warm every Sunday. Does she know her daughter is down here?
iris|Carmen is happy. Everyone at that table is happy.
steve|That’s not an answer, Nor.
iris|It is the only one I am allowed to give you.
steve|Lyle, do your boys know where you are tonight?
lyle_copy|They’re asleep. I’ll be at their game on Sunday. I always am now.
steve|You used to miss every single one.
lyle_copy|People change, Steve. Mostly for the better.
steve|You’re a deputy, Lyle. You swore an oath to this town.
lyle_copy|I did. I remember every word of it.
steve|Then get me out of this chair.
lyle_copy|I am helping you, Steve. This is the easy way.
